name: Bahrain Islamic Bank
founded: 1979 (incorporated by Amiri Decree No. 2 of 1979; Bahrain's first Islamic bank)
ownership_summary: National Bank of Bahrain (NBB) is the controlling shareholder: 80.22% at 30 Jun 2026 (31 Dec 2025: 78.81%) per BisB's interim statements, 80.23% on the Bahrain Bourse shareholder list. NBB first took control in 2020 (78.8% after its offer) and fully consolidates BisB. The only other holder above 5% is the Kuwait Awqaf Public Foundation (7.18% at 31 Dec 2025). Bahraini holders own 87.65% by nationality (31 Dec 2025).

shareholders.holder: Kuwait Awqaf Public Foundation (General Council of Kuwaiti Awqaf)

government_link: Indirect - controlled by NBB (80.2%), in which Bahrain Mumtalakat Holding Company holds 44.06% (see bh-nbb); the Kuwait Awqaf Public Foundation (7.18%) is described in the AR as a sovereign holder.
group_structure: BisB is a listed subsidiary of NBB (bh-nbb), which consolidates it in full (NBB 80.2% at 30 Jun 2026). NBB's group total assets, deposits and profit already include BisB, so never add the two. BisB keeps a separate CBB Islamic licence, balance sheet, Shari'a board and brand, while selected governance, operational and support functions are integrated with NBB (AR 2025). BisB's only subsidiary is Abaad Real Estate Company W.L.L. (100%). Its Vice Chairman is NBB Group CEO Usman Ahmed, and NBB executives Ali Ehsan and Husain Almohri sit on its board. NBB and BBK are in merger talks; BisB is not a party.
footprint: Bahrain only: six branches at 30 Jun 2026 (seven at 31 Dec 2025), plus digital channels (BisB Mobile, BisB Digital/eBISB, kiosks, contact centre, WhatsApp, chatbot). Registered office in Manama.
customer_segments: Retail (Bahraini nationals and residents, GCC citizens, youth, salary-linked Premium and Al Thuraya premium tiers), SMEs and corporates (incl. government-related entities), financial institutions, accredited investors for wealth products.
business_lines: Retail Banking (accounts, financing, cards, Premium and Al Thuraya); Corporate Banking (financing, trade, cash management, sukuk custody, supply-chain finance); Treasury/Investment Banking (Shari'a-compliant interbank, sukuk portfolio, FX, hedging, structured products) with a Wealth Management function launched in 2025; segment reporting uses Retail, Corporate, Market and Client Solutions and Others.

capabilities.wealth_summary: BisB is a small, fully Shari'a-compliant retail bank (BHD 1.78bn assets, six branches) that began building a wealth function in 2025 under its Treasury/Investment Banking unit. The 2025 annual report lists three launches: an Islamic credit-linked note linked to Bahrain's credit risk (first in the Kingdom, for accredited investors), a partnership with Societe Generale for 'world-class wealth management solutions', and a partnership with Allfunds to widen client access to global Shari'a-compliant fund managers within an 'open-architecture investment platform'; wealth-management revenue grew 'substantially' with green sukuk offerings. Client-facing tiers are Al Thuraya (premium/priority, Visa Infinite, dedicated RMs, 'exclusive Shari'a compliant investment products', no published threshold) and BisB Premium (salary of BD 1,500+ for three months). The BisB Mobile product page lists no investing features, and no AUM, brokerage or discretionary offer was found. NBB controls the bank (80.2%) and the NBB group is in merger talks with BBK.

digital_investing.detail: BisB Mobile page lists biometric sign-in, cardless withdrawal, transfers, card controls and budgeting/saving only; no in-app investing or wealth features. Retail digital adoption rose from 68% to 74% in 2025 with 91% digital onboarding.

funds_platform.detail: AR 2025: partnered with Allfunds to 'enhance our investment fund architecture' and widen access to global Shari'a-compliant fund managers, 'further strengthening our open-architecture investment platform'. Client-facing fund shelf not seen on BisB product pages; no press release found.

structured_products.detail: Shari'a-compliant Islamic credit-linked note linked to Bahrain's credit risk for accredited investors (2025); Treasury offers 'Sukuk and structured products'; partnership with Societe Generale for wealth solutions.

islamic_wealth.detail: Entire bank is Shari'a-compliant: sukuk portfolio (+47% in 2025), green sukuk offerings, Islamic credit-linked note, Shari'a fund access via Allfunds; 'Al Murshid' AI Shari'a platform launched 2025.

Partnered 'to offer investors world-class wealth management solutions' (AR 2025); product scope not detailed

initiatives.what: Wealth Management launched an Islamic credit-linked note (first in Bahrain, accredited investors); partnered with Societe Generale and Allfunds; introduced green sukuk offerings; Premium segment and Tejoori Premium savers launched in retail.
Launched 'Al Murshid', an AI-powered Shari'a knowledge platform; digital adoption up (retail 68% to 74%).
Husain Almohri (NBB Group CE Markets & Client Solutions) appointed to the BisB board as NBB representative.
H1 2026 results published: profit BHD 6.5m (H1 2025: 13.2m incl. one-off real-estate income); NBB's holding rose to 80.22%.
Appointment of a Head of Special Assets disclosed on the Bourse.
BisB became first bank to offer Shari'a-compliant financing through the consumer lending marketplace on BenefitPay (news listing).
Named 'Best Islamic Bank in Bahrain' at the Euromoney Islamic Finance Awards 2026 (news listing).

opportunities: Wealth Management function is new (2025) and describes an 'open-architecture investment platform' with Shari'a-compliant fund access via Allfunds (S3 p.21).
BisB's own product pages show no funds, sukuk or in-app investing for retail or Al Thuraya clients; Al Thuraya mentions only unnamed 'exclusive Shari'a compliant investment products' (S8, S9).
Retail digital adoption 74% and 91% digital onboarding in 2025 (S3 p.62) give a channel for digital investing, which the app does not yet offer.
barriers: Controlled by NBB (80.2%); NBB integrates selected governance, operational and support functions and its Markets & Client Solutions head sits on the BisB board, so vendor choices are likely made at group level (S2, S3, S13).
Allfunds (fund architecture) and Societe Generale (wealth solutions) are already named partners (S3 p.21).
NBB Group CEO and BisB Vice Chairman Usman Ahmed resigns by 31 Dec 2026 and NBB-BBK merger talks are open, adding group-level uncertainty (see bh-nbb).
Small balance sheet (BHD 1.78bn) and six branches; wealth revenue not disclosed in amounts.
